fields.reasoning: Same root cause as #417 (code-check-leaves-reference-to-self-check): the daemon's in-process check is the installed binary, so a run whose change bumps entry.FormatVersion can never pass review/code until merged and installed. That Decision rejected building the worktree's binary in the code check (generic across projects, Go toolchain and CPU cost on the shared VM) and leaned on make self-check, which builds the branch and runs in CI before every merge; the same reasoning holds here, so newer-format entries are left to it. Limiting the tolerance to entries the branch adds keeps the check honest for the case where the installed binary is genuinely behind main. build-check already folds without the unreadable entries (store.ReadLog keeps them as problems), and a builder writes Evidence at the lowest format that spells it, so leaving them out of the fold does not hide a verifier's Evidence.
fields.statement: Change set 01M732D2 serves m4-runs-hold-up, as earlier run-repair change sets do. The run code check (internal/api/run_codecheck.go checkIn/runCheck) stops failing a log entry that declares a newer format than the installed binary reads (entry.ErrNewerFormat) when the run's branch adds that entry since its merge-base: such an entry is reported as a warning, not a cause. A newer-format entry already at the merge-base, and every other unreadable or invalid entry, still fails. The code check sets this through an explicit CheckRequest option, so plain rhiza check and make self-check are unchanged and still judge every entry with the branch's own build in CI before merge. The code check does not build the run worktree's binary.

fields.acceptance: A testscript in a run worktree whose branch commits an entry with v one above entry.FormatVersion sees rhiza check fail on it and rhiza run code-check pass with no cause naming it; the same entry committed before the merge-base makes run code-check fail naming it; a test of the check op shows the option off still fails the branch's newer-format entry (go test -trimpath ./internal/api/... ./internal/check/... and the touched testscripts; describe-golden regenerated if CheckRequest changes)
fields.statement: rhiza run code-check does not fail a log entry of a newer format than the installed binary reads when the run's branch adds it since its merge-base, reporting it as a warning instead, through an explicit CheckRequest option, so a run whose change bumps the entry format can pass review/code; newer-format entries at the merge-base and every other bad entry still fail, and plain rhiza check and make self-check keep failing every newer-format entry
